packets.name: Ashley Edwards / Missouri Department of Conservation

messages.subject: A story from Missouri’s first-time women’s deer hunt
messages.body_text:
Hi Ashley,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we’re building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma and reaching into nearby hunting communities.

I saw the October 10–11 mentored hunt for first-time women at Prairie Fork. The mix of classroom preparation, an experienced mentor and accessible equipment could make a powerful first-hunt story.

After the hunt, would you be willing to pass an invitation to one participant and mentor who want to talk about what the experience meant? They can contact me directly. We would get their permission before sharing anything.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

reasons: The current Missouri program combines first-hunt education, one-to-one mentorship and accessible equipment, creating a strong nearby-community story while keeping participant contact and permission with the organizer.

profile.background: Missouri Department of Conservation is the state wildlife agency. Its Prairie Fork program is for first-time female deer hunters age 18 or older. The September 1, 2026 announcement sets the hunt for October 10-11 and describes instruction, experienced mentors and available mobility equipment.
profile.goal: Hear an adult woman and mentor describe the preparation, confidence and personal meaning of a first deer hunt; have Ashley pass the invitation after the event.
profile.status: Ashley agreed to the requested invitation. No participant has agreed and no interview is booked in the retrieved conversation.
profile.next_step: Prepare an approved, short invitation for Ashley to pass after October 11. State the proposed use and let interested adults contact Craig.
questions: What did the participant find most difficult before the hunt?
What did the mentor do that changed her confidence?
What stayed with her afterward, including if no deer was harvested?
profile.verification: Key program facts checked at the original source October 8, 2026
profile.caution: This is an adult women's program, not a youth hunt.

messages.subject: Your Lincoln County deer hunt and first-hunt stories
messages.body_text:
Hi Bobby,

I’m Craig Ramos with Whitetail Syndicate. I saw the Lincoln County deer hunt on your Oklahoma calendar for October 17. The relationship between a young hunter, their family, and a mentor feels like a story worth hearing beyond the result of the hunt.

Would you be open to a short conversation about how you prepare a family for that day? If a mentor or family later wants to tell their own story, we would ask them directly and get permission before sharing anything, especially involving a young hunter.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: The hunters behind Pine Tree's October 10 cleanup
messages.body_text:
Hi Charles,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real people and stories behind whitetail hunting.

I saw the October 10 cleanup at Pine Tree WDA. I'd like to hear from someone who hunts there and gives their time to keep it in good shape. The work people do for a place, and the hunting memories they have there, seem worth keeping together.

Would you be open to a short conversation, or pointing me to a willing volunteer? We'd work around the cleanup and ask permission before sharing anyone's story.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: The hunt behind a donated deer
messages.body_text:
Hi Darren,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

Your Share the Harvest piece in the fall United Bowhunter stood out, especially the part about a donated deer helping someone close to home. That gives the hunt a story that carries on after the deer is brought out of the woods.

Would you be open to a short conversation about a deer hunt you chose to donate and what made you do it? We'd ask permission before using any story, photo or recording.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: Greg: the parent-child story at Cross Bell Ranch
messages.body_text:
Hi Greg,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail hunting stories.

Your account of the girls taking over the butchering lesson at the daddy-daughter event caught my attention. With the October 14–18 parent-child event at Cross Bell Ranch coming up, I'd like to hear how learning to hunt, process a doe, and cook it together changes what that hunt means to a family.

Would you be open to a short conversation, or passing this to a willing parent? We'd work around the event and get the family's permission, including a parent or guardian for any youth story, before sharing anything.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate
messages.body_html:
Hi Greg,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail hunting stories.

Your account of the girls taking over the butchering lesson at the daddy-daughter event caught my attention. With the October 14–18 parent-child event at Cross Bell Ranch coming up, I'd like to hear how learning to hunt, process a doe, and cook it together changes what that hunt means to a family.

Would you be open to a short conversation, or passing this to a willing parent? We'd work around the event and get the family's permission, including a parent or guardian for any youth story, before sharing anything.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

Hello Peel Compton team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. The Quiver's lessons and 3D practice give new archers a place to build confidence before deer season. I'd like to explore telling one willing beginner's story from the range to an ethical first hunt, including the preparation and uncertainty along the way.

Could you route this to the person who works with The Quiver's archery programs? I'd be glad to talk through a small, respectful story project.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A story from the East Texas youth whitetail hunt
messages.body_text:
Hello Blast & Cast team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. I saw the East Texas youth whitetail and hog hunt scheduled for October 30–November 1. The time a father, son, and volunteer mentor spend together—at the range, in the blind, and learning to process a deer—could make a meaningful story.

Would your East Texas chapter be open to discussing a story with a willing family and volunteer? We would follow your guidance and seek the family's permission first.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

Would you be willing to pass this invitation to a mentor and family who want to share one of those stories? We would work through your team and the parent or guardian and get permission before using any story or pictures.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: Whitetail Deer Adventures on October 19
messages.body_text:
Hello Searcy County 4-H team,

I saw the Whitetail Deer Adventures sessions planned for October 19 in Oxley and Leslie, with lessons about deer habitat and scoring antlers.

I’m Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the memories and people behind deer hunting. I wondered whether a local hunter’s story about a meaningful deer, including a hunt that didn’t end with a harvest, could add something to that discussion beyond the score. Would the event organizer be open to a short conversation about the idea? I’d follow your guidance on what is appropriate for the youth program.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A story after the BOW fall weekend
messages.body_text:
Hi Lea,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. I saw the October 2–4 Becoming an Outdoors-Woman weekend at Lake Conway. For someone who leaves with new hunting or archery skills, the next step toward a first deer season can be as meaningful as the class itself.

Would you be open to discussing a willing participant's story as she prepares for a hunt? We'd coordinate through the program and get her permission before recording or sharing anything.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: The story behind your Colcord Making Memories hunt
messages.body_text:
Hi Logan,

I saw the Making Memories deer hunt you’re bringing to Colcord November 28–29, including the plan to pair adaptive hunters with guides and the call for photographers and mentors.

I’m Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around real whitetail stories. The moment a hunter meets their guide, gets back into the woods, and tells the story afterward feels worth preserving. Would you be open to a short conversation about whether we could help tell one of those stories, with the hunter’s permission and in a way that supports your event?

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate
messages.body_html:
Hi Logan,

I saw the Making Memories deer hunt you’re bringing to Colcord November 28–29, including the plan to pair adaptive hunters with guides and the call for photographers and mentors.

messages.subject: A story from the Searcy youth deer hunt
messages.body_text:
Hi Opie,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail hunting stories.

I saw the Searcy chapter's November 6–8 youth deer hunt at Two Rivers Hunt Club in Georgetown. I'd like to hear how a volunteer and family get ready for that weekend and what the experience means to them, whether or not a deer is harvested.

Would you be open to a short conversation, or passing this along to the Searcy chapter? We'd work around the hunt and only share a story with the family's permission and your guidance.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: The people keeping Timmy's deer hunt going
messages.body_text:
Hello Missouri Disabled Sportsmen team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the people and stories behind whitetail hunting.

I saw the December 11–13 Timmy "Taters" Smith memorial hunt in Leonard. I'd like to hear how the volunteers have kept his memory going through this hunt, and what the time with a mentor means to a participant.

Would someone be open to a short conversation? If there's a hunter or volunteer who wants to share their experience, we'd follow your guidance and get their permission first, including a parent or guardian for a youth story.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: Story invitation for the Millwood youth deer-hunt team
messages.body_text:
Hi there,

Could you pass this to the Millwood Tri-Lakes youth deer-hunt team?

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we’re building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I saw the November 7–8 youth hunt announcement and the support you’re providing with access, blinds and adult guidance. I’d love to hear a mentor’s perspective on what helps a young hunter feel ready for that first hunt.

Would someone on the team be open to a short conversation? Any family participation would go through the organizer and parent, with permission before anything is shared.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: Your mentored doe hunt and a hunter story
messages.body_text:
Hello Oklahoma Hunters & Anglers team,

I saw your December mentored doe hunt at Tatanka Ranch in Stroud. Pairing a new hunter one on one with a mentor feels like the sort of experience whose story stays with people well beyond that first deer.

I’m building Whitetail Syndicate around the people, memories, and community of whitetail hunting. Would someone on your team be open to a short conversation about what new hunters need and how this hunt came together? If a mentor or participant later wants to share their story, we would ask them directly for permission.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A hunter-to-table story with AHFH
messages.body_text:
Hello AHFH team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. Your work gives a harvest a second story once the deer leaves camp. I'd like to explore following one donated deer from a willing hunter through a participating processor and into the local feeding effort.

Would someone on your team be willing to talk about how to tell that story accurately, with consent from everyone involved and without disrupting the donation process?

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

first_message.subject: A hunter-to-table story with AHFH
first_message.body_text:
Hello AHFH team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. Your work gives a harvest a second story once the deer leaves camp. I'd like to explore following one donated deer from a willing hunter through a participating processor and into the local feeding effort.

Would someone on your team be willing to talk about how to tell that story accurately, with consent from everyone involved and without disrupting the donation process?

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A deer weekend that brings a family back together
messages.body_text:
Hi Shawn,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I saw that Darby's Youth Hunting Program gives service members and their children a chance to reconnect through deer weekends that begin on the range and move into the field. That feels like a story about much more than the harvest.

Would you be open to a short conversation, or willing to pass this invitation to a parent and guide who may want to share their experience? We would work through your organization and the parent or guardian and ask permission before using any story, photo or recording.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A deer-hunting storytelling invitation after the contest
messages.body_text:
Hi Virginia,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we’re building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I saw the My Natural State Story contest and its hunting category. The focus on why an outdoor experience mattered is close to the stories we hope to hear.

Once the contest wraps up, would it be appropriate to pass an invitation to a willing parent and student with a meaningful deer-hunting experience? They could contact me directly if interested. We’d talk with the parent first and get permission before sharing anything.

I’m not requesting student details or contest submissions. If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: The story behind a Dan Fout Memorial deer hunt
messages.body_text:
Hi William,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we’re building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma and reaching into other hunting communities too.

I saw this fall’s Dan Fout Memorial hunts and the way volunteers help veterans get into the deer woods. I’d love to hear about one hunt where the time together meant as much as the deer.

Would you be open to sharing a story from your own experience, or passing the invitation to a willing veteran and volunteer? They could contact me directly. We would talk first and get permission before sharing anything.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A first-deer story from 273 Outdoors
messages.body_text:
Hi Chris,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we’re building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I came across 273 Outdoors and the hunting and fishing mentorship you offer young men. I’d love to hear about a first deer hunt where the relationship with a mentor mattered more than filling the tag.

Would you or a willing mentor be open to sharing one of those experiences? If a young hunter is involved, we’d go through you and their parent or guardian. We would talk first and get permission before sharing any story or pictures.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: Your column on continuing to hunt with a deer allergy
messages.body_text:
Hi Al,

Your October 3 column about being allergic to deer and continuing to hunt stayed with me. I was struck by the question of what keeps a hunter going when the experience itself becomes more complicated.

I’m building Whitetail Syndicate around honest whitetail stories and the people behind them. Would you be open to a short conversation about that part of your experience? I’d seek your permission before quoting or publishing anything.

Thanks for considering it,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

first_message.subject: Your column on continuing to hunt with a deer allergy
first_message.body_text:
Hi Al,

Your October 3 column about being allergic to deer and continuing to hunt stayed with me. I was struck by the question of what keeps a hunter going when the experience itself becomes more complicated.

I’m building Whitetail Syndicate around honest whitetail stories and the people behind them. Would you be open to a short conversation about that part of your experience? I’d seek your permission before quoting or publishing anything.

Thanks for considering it,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Alexis Nunan / Hero-Hunts Foundation

messages.subject: A veteran and guide story from the 2026 Hero-Hunts deer hunt
messages.body_text:
Hi Alexis,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we’re building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma and reaching into other hunting communities.

I saw the November 21 Hero-Hunts deer hunt and the way it brings veterans, volunteer guides and landowners together for a day in the woods. I’d like to hear about a hunt where the connection between those people mattered as much as the harvest.

Would you be open to a short conversation, or willing to pass this invitation to a veteran and guide who want to tell their story? We would speak with them first and get permission before sharing any story or pictures.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Anderson Dingus / Whitetails Unlimited, Lonoke County

messages.subject: Lonoke County chapter's October 10 gathering
messages.body_text:
Hi Anderson,

I’m Craig Ramos with Whitetail Syndicate. I saw the Lonoke County chapter’s October 10 banquet and your role as Whitetails Unlimited’s Arkansas field director. We’re collecting real whitetail stories from local hunters and the volunteers who bring them together.

Would you be willing to connect me with Kim or another Lonoke chapter volunteer for a short conversation about the chapter and the stories its members tell? I’m interested in listening first and would ask each hunter directly before sharing their words or photos.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: The stories behind Antlers’ Mount Bragging wall
messages.body_text:
Hi Monica and Deer Festival team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. I saw this year's Antlers Deer Festival and the Mount Bragging wall. I'd love to hear how one of those hunters remembers the hunt beyond the mount itself, and possibly explore a small story-recording presence at a future festival.

Would you be open to a conversation about connecting with a willing participant from this year's show and what a future collaboration might look like?

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Arkansas Big Buck Classic

messages.subject: Recording Arkansas hunt stories at the 2027 Big Buck Classic
messages.body_text:
Hello Big Buck Classic team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. Your January 22–24 show brings Arkansas hunters together to celebrate the stories behind their deer. I'm exploring a simple story-recording presence where willing attendees could tell a short account of the hunt they still talk about—whether or not it produced a big rack.

Could we discuss whether that fits the 2027 event and what a small vendor or collaborative setup would require?

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Ashley Eve Wildlife Taxidermy

messages.subject: The story behind a finished deer mount
messages.body_text:
Hi Ashley,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we’re building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I saw that you’re taking new work again in 2026. A taxidermist meets hunters at a part of the story most people never see, when the excitement of the hunt turns into deciding how the memory will be preserved.

Is there a deer mount from your own experience that still stands out, or a willing customer you could pass this invitation to? They can contact me directly. We would talk first and get permission before sharing any story or pictures.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Austin and Charles / The Whitetail Distraction Podcast

messages.subject: A whitetail story you still tell at camp
messages.body_text:
Austin and Charles,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I came across your September 21 porch episode with Joey Flynn and the bowhunting stories behind it. That is the kind of conversation we're looking for: a hunt that people keep retelling long after the season ends, whether they got the deer or missed their chance.

Would either of you be open to a short conversation about one whitetail hunt you still talk about at camp? We'd ask permission before using any story, photo or recording.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Bear Grease / MeatEater

messages.subject: Aaron Stanphill’s Arkansas public-land story
messages.body_text:
Hello Bear Grease team,

I listened to the September 30 discussion of Aaron Stanphill’s Arkansas public-land roots and his first Pope & Young buck after thirty years. The long arc of that story, especially how he learned to hunt, is what caught my attention.

I’m building Whitetail Syndicate as a community for whitetail hunters to share the stories behind their hunts. If Aaron is open to it, would you be willing to pass along an invitation for a short conversation? I’d love to hear what that buck meant after all those years and would get his permission before sharing any of his story.

Thank you,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Big H Hunts

messages.subject: A whitetail story shared across generations
messages.body_text:
Hi Big H Hunts team,

I’m Craig Ramos, building Whitetail Syndicate as a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

Your 2026-27 whitetail page puts real emphasis on sharing the outdoors with the next generation. That is exactly the kind of experience I’m looking to understand: the family or guide who remembers the time together more than the size of the buck.

Would someone on your guide team, or a willing family from camp, be open to a short conversation about one of those hunts? Please let them decide whether to contact me. We would only use a story, image, or recording with their direct permission.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Blue Sage Outfitters

messages.subject: Building Blue Sage from a lifetime in northwest Oklahoma
messages.body_text:
Hi Blue Sage team,

I’m Craig Ramos with Whitetail Syndicate. I saw that Blue Sage started in 2025 and is taking hunters into the 2026 season around Woodward, including a youth rifle hunt. I’d love to hear how a lifetime of hunting that country turned into the outfitting business.

Would the owner be open to a short conversation about that start and a hunt that captures what Blue Sage is trying to build? We’re collecting real hunter stories and would get permission before sharing any client’s experience or images.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Bobby Armstrong / Po’Folk Outdoors

messages.subject: The deer-camp story behind a first trophy
messages.body_text:
Hi Bobby,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we’re building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I came across Po’Folk Outdoors and your approach to deer camp: family, friendships and celebrating what a trophy means to that particular hunter. That’s the kind of story we’re interested in.

Is there a hunt from your own experience where a new hunter’s first deer meant more than the antler size? I’d love to hear what happened and what made it stay with you. We would talk first and get permission before sharing any story or pictures.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A hunting story someone wants to pass along
messages.body_text:
Hello Wildlife Conservation team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail hunting stories.

I saw the October 16–18 youth hunt and October 24–26 Cherokee Speaker Hunt at Sequoyah. I'd like to hear from someone who wants to share a hunting memory and what they choose to pass along to the next generation.

Would your department be open to a short conversation, or pointing me to the right person? We'd follow your guidance on cultural and story permissions and ask each person before sharing anything.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

first_message.subject: A hunting story someone wants to pass along
first_message.body_text:
Hello Wildlife Conservation team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail hunting stories.

I saw the October 16–18 youth hunt and October 24–26 Cherokee Speaker Hunt at Sequoyah. I'd like to hear from someone who wants to share a hunting memory and what they choose to pass along to the next generation.

Would your department be open to a short conversation, or pointing me to the right person? We'd follow your guidance on cultural and story permissions and ask each person before sharing anything.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Clifton Denney / On Your Own Outdoors

messages.subject: Question about one of your Arkansas hunts
messages.body_text:
Clifton,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate. I came across On Your Own Outdoors and the public-land hunts you share in Arkansas.

We’re putting together real stories from whitetail hunters. I’m interested in the hunt somebody still talks about, whether they got the deer, missed it, or something else happened that stuck with them.

Is there one of your own hunts you’d be open to telling me about? I’d like to hear it from you first, then we could talk about whether it makes sense to do a full story.

If it’s not a fit, no problem. I won’t keep emailing you.

Craig Ramos

messages.subject: The story behind your Arkansas venison donation
messages.body_text:
Hi Cypress Valley team,

I'm Craig Ramos with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we're building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I saw your part in the venison donation on The Element's August 20 episode, "Filling Freezers Buck Truck Style." I'd like to hear what that effort meant to the people doing the processing and helping feed neighbors.

Would someone involved be open to a short conversation about one moment they remember? We'd ask permission before using any story, image or recording, and respect the privacy of anyone receiving food.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: David Hinceman / Hands of a Sportsman

messages.subject: A story from one of your 2026 youth deer hunts
messages.body_text:
David,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I saw the two 2026 youth deer hunts Hands of a Sportsman is helping host in Stanly County for young hunters who have never harvested a deer. I'd like to hear about a day when a guide saw something click for a young hunter, whether the hunt ended with a deer or simply a memory they carried home.

Would you be willing to pass this invitation to a guide and family who may want to talk? We would work through your organization and the parent or guardian, and ask permission before using any story, photo or recording.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: The people behind your deer hunts
messages.body_text:
Hi Nathan, Isaac, and the VETDD214 team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand rooted in real whitetail stories. We're starting with Arkansas and Oklahoma and getting to know people keeping that hunting community going.

I read how an uncle and nephew's conversation on a Mississippi back road became VETDD214. I'd like to hear how that idea turned into your deer hunts, and what a day in the field with your group means to the people who come.

Would someone be open to a short conversation? If a participant wants to share a memorable hunt, we'd follow your guidance and ask their permission before sharing anything.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Dr. Mark Turner / Blazin’ Grazin’ and Other Wild Things

messages.subject: The whitetail story behind years of habitat work
messages.body_text:
Hi Dr. Turner,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around real whitetail hunting stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I came across your June 30 Blazin' Grazin' and Other Wild Things episode about summer forbs and native deer forage. It made me think about a hunter who spent years improving a place before a memorable hunt finally came together.

Would you be open to a short conversation about the human side of that work, or passing this invitation to a willing Oklahoma hunter or landowner? I'd like to hear what changed on the land, what they learned, and why that hunt mattered to them. We'd get permission before sharing anything and respect your recordings and research.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Duane Hada / Cross Trail Outfitters Buffalo River

messages.subject: A Buffalo River deer-hunt story
messages.body_text:
Hi Duane,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we’re building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I read about the Buffalo River chapter and how you use hunting, outdoor skills and mentorship to help young men build lasting friendships. I’m interested in a deer hunt that shows what having someone alongside them meant to a new hunter.

Is there one from your own experience you’d be open to telling me about? If a family wants to take part, we’d go through you and the parent or guardian. Nothing would be shared without permission.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A story from Duck Creek's work days
messages.body_text:
Hi Duck Creek team,

I’m Craig Ramos with Whitetail Syndicate. I saw that your club brings families into the membership and asks members to put in work days. That sounds like a big part of what makes a deer camp more than a place to hunt.

Would someone who helps run the club be open to a short conversation about those work days and a season or member story that has stuck with you? We’re collecting real whitetail stories told by the people who were there, and would ask permission before sharing anyone’s words or photos.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: An Arkansas urban bowhunt story
messages.body_text:
Hi Dwayne,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. I saw the 2026–27 urban archery hunts and the work that goes into qualifying hunters, keeping these hunts safe, and putting venison to use. I'd love to document a first-year participant's experience from preparation through a hunt, if they and your association are willing.

Could we talk briefly about whether there is a responsible way to tell that story without interfering with the program?

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

Would he be open to a short conversation, or passing this invitation to someone who wants to tell their story? We'd ask permission before sharing anything and respect your recordings and photos.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos

Thanks,

messages.subject: A family hunting story from Fort Rock
messages.body_text:
Hi Fort Rock team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around real whitetail hunting stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

Your family camp and Hunt Camp caught my attention. I'd like to hear about a parent and beginner hunter learning together: what they were nervous about, how a mentor helped, and the memory they took home, whether or not they got a deer.

Would someone be open to a short conversation, or passing this invitation to a willing family? We'd follow your guidance, work around camp activities, and get permission from the family and a parent or guardian before sharing any youth story or photo.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Greg Allen / Bend of the River Outfitters

messages.subject: Greg, a question about a hunt that stuck with you
messages.body_text:
Greg,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate. I came across Bend of the River Outfitters and your western Oklahoma whitetail hunts.

We’re talking with hunters about the hunt they still tell people about. It doesn’t have to be a trophy deer or even a successful shot. Sometimes the story is the people, the place, or what happened when the plan changed.

Is there one of your own hunts you’d be willing to tell me about? I’d like to hear it first before we talk about doing anything with the story.

If it’s not a fit, no problem. I won’t keep emailing you.

Craig Ramos

packets.name: HardWood Outdoors

messages.subject: Todd's unforgettable buck story
messages.body_text:
Hi Hard Wood Outdoors team,

I read Todd Self’s account on your guest stories page: after he tagged his buck, a larger buck pushed the downed deer downhill, EP brought another hunter over, and that hunter missed in the excitement. It’s the kind of story people tell for years.

I’m Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around real whitetail hunting memories, including the imperfect moments. Would you be open to a short conversation about the stories that come out of your camp? If Todd were interested in telling the full version, I’d ask for his permission directly through you. There’s no need to share his contact information.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: The story behind a trailing-dog recovery
messages.body_text:
Hi HuntDog team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. I came across your handler-centered trailing-dog program and noticed your 2026 training spots are full. Most hunters see the successful recovery, but rarely the training, judgment, and trust between a handler and dog that make it possible.

Would you be interested in a short conversation about telling a real recovery story, including what the hunter and handler learned along the way? We'd only share a case everyone involved is comfortable discussing.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.body_text:
Hi Hunters Advantage team,

I came across your August 24 episode with Jordan Shofler about mountain bucks on northeast Oklahoma public land. I’d like to hear the story of one hunt where all that scouting finally made sense, or a missed chance that changed how he hunted afterward.

Would you be willing to pass this invitation to Jordan? He can contact me directly if interested. We would talk first and get permission before sharing anything.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

Would you be up for a brief conversation about sharing a processor's perspective or one willing customer's memorable hunt this season? I'd like to give that after-the-shot work the attention it deserves.

Craig Ramos

messages.subject: A veteran whitetail story from Christoval
messages.body_text:
Hi Hunting with Soldiers team,

I’m Craig Ramos, building Whitetail Syndicate as a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I saw your October 2026 Christoval hunt is bringing three combat veterans together for a whitetail weekend, with meals and housing handled so they can focus on the experience. I’d like to hear what a weekend like that means to the people involved, beyond the deer itself.

Would an organizer or a willing veteran be open to a short conversation after the hunt? You’re welcome to forward this invitation rather than share anyone’s contact information. We would only use a story, image, or recording with that person’s direct permission.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

We’re talking with hunters about the hunts that stayed with them. A first deer, a missed shot, or a day with family can make a better story than the size of the buck.

Is there one from your own experience you’d be open to telling me about? We would talk first. I wouldn’t use anyone’s name, pictures, or account without a separate conversation and permission.

If this isn’t for you, no problem. I won’t keep emailing you.

messages.body_text:
Hi John,

I’m Craig Ramos with Whitetail Syndicate. Your October trip in Combs caught my attention: a small group hunting Ozark public land, with friendship and faith at the center of the camp.

Would you be open to a short conversation about why you put this trip together and what you hope the men take home besides a hunt? We’re gathering real stories around whitetail hunting and the people it brings together. If participants later want to share their own experiences, we would ask them directly for permission.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: John Burk / Missouri Governor's Mentored Deer Hunt

messages.subject: A story from Missouri's Governor's Mentored Deer Hunt
messages.body_text:
Hi John,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand we’re building around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma and reaching into nearby hunting communities.

I saw that Missouri’s Governor’s Mentored Deer Hunt is happening October 9 through 11 and gives preference to people who have never hunted or harvested a deer. I’d like to hear what a first hunt means to a new hunter and the mentor beside them.

Would you be open to a short conversation after the hunt, or willing to pass this invitation to a mentor and participant who want to share their experience? For any youth story, we would work through the organizer and parent or guardian, and we would get permission before sharing anything.

If it’s not a fit, no problem.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A meaningful deer-hunt story from Mission 4:19
messages.body_text:
Hi Jon,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail hunting stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I saw the twelve veterans you've hosted during deer season and your focus on relationships that last beyond a hunt. I'd like to hear about one participant and guide: how they prepared, the moments that brought them together, and what they carried home from the woods.

Would you be open to a short conversation, or passing this invitation to a willing veteran, first responder, or volunteer? They can choose what they want to discuss. We'd work around your programs, follow your guidance, and get permission before sharing any story or photo.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Julie / Hunters for the Hungry Louisiana

messages.subject: A whitetail story from the hunt to feeding neighbors
messages.body_text:
Hi Julie,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around real whitetail stories and the people behind them.

I saw the updated processor network and the 19,465 pounds collected through this year's Freezer Day. I'd like to hear one story that follows a donated deer from the hunter, through the processor, to helping feed neighbors.

Would you be open to a short conversation, and possibly connecting me with a willing hunter and processor? We'd follow your guidance and get permission before sharing anything, especially anything involving the people receiving food.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: Luke Clayton

messages.subject: The story behind your return to Choctaw Hunting Lodge
messages.body_text:
Hi Luke,

I read your October 5 piece about heading back to Choctaw Hunting Lodge with Larry Weishuhn. What caught me was that this is a place you return to, and the people and traditions around a repeat hunt can be as memorable as the deer.

I’m building Whitetail Syndicate as a home for whitetail hunters’ stories. Would you be open to a brief conversation after this trip about what draws you back and what happened in camp? I’d ask permission before sharing any part of it.

Best,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: Would you pass a note to Keener and Sons Hunting Club?
messages.body_text:
Hi Daxton,

I saw the AGFC recognize Lynn Keener and Sons Hunting Club as its 2026 DMAP Deer Club of the Year. Their habitat work in the face of CWD seems like a story other Arkansas deer clubs could learn from.

I’m Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the people and experiences behind whitetail hunting. If you work with the Keener family, would you be willing to pass along my interest in talking with a club member about the changes they made, what they observed, and what the family has learned? They can reach me by replying to this email if they’re interested. No need to share their contact details with me.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

Thanks,

packets.name: North American Whitetail / Derek Curtis inquiry

messages.subject: A note for Derek Curtis about Curly Brow
messages.body_text:
Hi Haynes,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I read Clifford Neames's September 2 article about Derek Curtis and Curly Brow. Hunting that narrow strip of woods where he played as a kid, then passing two mature bucks while waiting for the one he'd watched all summer, gives that hunt a story beyond the rack.

Would you be willing to pass this note to Clifford or Derek? I'd welcome a short conversation about his connection to that place and the decisions on opening morning. We'd get Derek's permission before sharing anything and respect your article and photo rights.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

Would someone on your team be open to a short conversation about helping a new bowhunter get ready for a first deer season? If a customer has a story they want to tell, you can forward this note and let them choose whether to reach out. We would ask their permission directly before using anything.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A family’s first Oklahoma deer hunt
messages.body_text:
Hello OYHP team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. I appreciate that your youth deer hunts bring a parent or guardian into the experience too, especially for families without a hunting background. That first weekend can change how both generations see the outdoors.

Would you be open to discussing a story with a willing family and mentor this season, from preparation and camp through the hunt and what they take home? We would work through your team and obtain the family's permission first.

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A beginner and mentor's story from Uwharrie deer camp
messages.body_text:
Hi Opportunity Outdoors team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around the people and stories behind whitetail hunting.

I saw your November 20–22 deer camp in Uwharrie. I'd like to hear how a mentor helps a beginner read deer sign and choose a setup on public land. There's a story in what they learn and who they meet, even if they go home with an unfilled tag.

Would someone be open to a short conversation about the camp, and possibly connecting us with a willing mentor and beginner? We'd ask their permission before sharing their story and work around your plans for the camp.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: Who handles story inquiries about Quapaw's deer season?
messages.body_text:
Hello Quapaw Nation Public Relations team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the people, traditions, and memories behind whitetail hunting, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I saw your October 1 deer-season announcement and the new Wildlife Code and harvest check-in tools. I'd welcome a short conversation with the appropriate wildlife or communications representative about responsible harvest reporting and the hunting traditions the Nation chooses to share.

Could you point me to the right person, or pass this invitation along? If a hunter or mentor later wants to tell a story, we'd follow the Nation's guidance and obtain their permission before sharing any names, photos, or stories.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: Question for the Red Rock whitetail guides
messages.body_text:
Hi Red Rock team,

I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate. I saw your northern Oklahoma whitetail hunts and the guides behind them.

We’re putting together real hunter stories, told by the people who lived them. Does someone on your guide team have a whitetail hunt they still talk about, whether it ended with a deer or not? I’d be glad to hear it in a short conversation before discussing a full story.

If one of your hunters might be interested, you could forward this to them and let them decide whether to contact me. I’m not asking for their information.

If this isn’t a fit, no problem. I won’t keep emailing you.

Craig Ramos

messages.subject: A story from the farm side of Rockin 69
messages.body_text:

I’m Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the people and memories behind whitetail hunting. I’d be interested in hearing why some hunters choose the farms and whether one of them might want to tell the story of a hunt that mattered to them, whatever the antler size.

Would you be open to a short conversation?

Thanks,
Craig Ramos

first_message.subject: A story from the farm side of Rockin 69
first_message.body_text:
Hi Rusty,

I saw that Rockin 69 gives hunters a choice between the managed big ranch and the smaller farms without antler minimums. That seems like it would lead to very different hunting stories.

I’m Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the people and memories behind whitetail hunting. I’d be interested in hearing why some hunters choose the farms and whether one of them might want to tell the story of a hunt that mattered to them, whatever the antler size.

Would you be open to a short conversation?

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.body_text:

We’re looking for real hunts to tell in the hunter’s own words. It could be a buck taken, a close call, or the one that got away. Does anyone on your guide team have a story like that they’d be open to talking through with me?

I’d start with a conversation and only discuss a full story if everyone is comfortable with it. If this isn’t for you, no problem. I won’t keep emailing you.

Craig Ramos

packets.name: Safari Club International / Women Go Hunting

messages.subject: Could you pass a note to Beullah Arrends Terrell?
messages.body_text:
Hello Safari editorial team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I read Beullah Arrends Terrell's October 2 story, "A Zulu Deer Hunter in Arkansas." The part that stayed with me was learning the crossbow alongside her husband, then finding that time in the woods had become part of her life.

Would you be willing to pass this note to her, or the Women Go Hunting team? I'd welcome a short conversation about becoming a hunter and what helped her feel confident getting started. We'd ask her permission before sharing anything. I'm happy for her to decide whether to contact me directly.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A mentor's story from the Plum Creek youth hunt
messages.body_text:
Hi Scott,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I saw your 2026 Plum Creek youth hunt listing and how the mentors accompany young longbow and recurve hunters without hunting themselves. I'd like to hear about a moment when that guidance changed a young hunter's experience, whether they came home with a deer or not.

Would you be willing to pass this invitation to a mentor and parent who want to share a story? They can contact me directly. We'd work through your team and the parent or guardian and get permission before using any story, photo or recording.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: Ozark whitetail stories worth keeping
messages.body_text:
Hi Ozark Podcast team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate around the real stories and people behind whitetail hunting. I like how your show lets ordinary Ozark people explain their connection to the land in their own words. We're finding Arkansas and Oklahoma hunters with stories that go deeper than the rack photo, including the hunt they missed or still talk about years later.

Would y'all be interested in comparing notes on a guest or a small shared story series this deer season?

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

packets.name: TRAKR

messages.subject: A story behind an Arkansas or Oklahoma deer recovery
messages.body_text:
Hi TRAKR team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand rooted in real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma.

I came across your Arkansas Blood Trailing Network and Oklahoma pages. A recovery has a whole story behind it: the hunter's uncertainty, the handler's judgment, and the work between a dog and its handler.

Would someone be open to a short conversation, or helping connect us with a willing Arkansas or Oklahoma tracking team? I'd like to hear about one memorable recovery and what it taught the people involved. We'd ask everyone involved before sharing their story.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

I'm Craig Ramos, building Whitetail Syndicate as a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories, starting in Arkansas and Oklahoma and reaching into neighboring hunting communities.

I saw your 2026 deer dates and the emphasis on lodging, meals and time together at deer camp. I'd like to hear from a guide or willing guest about a memorable hunt whose meaning came from the camp and the people as much as the deer.

Would someone be open to a short conversation, or pass this invitation to an adult guest? We would ask permission before using any story, photo or recording.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

messages.subject: A note for Jordan about Graham Smith's hunt story
messages.body_text:
Hi WCB team,

I'm Craig Ramos, helping build Whitetail Syndicate, a clothing and community brand around real whitetail stories.

I came across Hunting The Mason Dixon's October 2 episode with Graham Smith. The years of history with that central North Carolina buck, ending on opening weekend, caught my attention. I'd like to hear what those seasons of watching and waiting meant to him, beyond the final score.

Would you be willing to pass this to Jordan Jones, and possibly Graham if he's interested? I'd welcome a short conversation. We'd ask permission before sharing a story and respect your episode and recording rights.

Thanks,
Craig Ramos
Whitetail Syndicate

sent_emails.subject: Question about one of your Arkansas hunts
sent_emails.body:
Clifton,
I’m Craig Ramos, working with Whitetail Syndicate. I came across On Your Own Outdoors and the public-land hunts you share in Arkansas.
We’re putting together real stories from whitetail hunters. I’m interested in the hunt somebody still talks about, whether they got the deer, missed it, or something else happened that stuck with them.
Is there one of your own hunts you’d be open to telling me about? I’d like to hear it from you first, then we could talk about whether it makes sense to do a full story.
If it’s not a fit, no problem. I won’t keep emailing you.
Craig Ramos
